name: Taenia spp.

taxonomy.rank_note: Reference groups can include multiple species. Protozoan higher-rank systems differ; the lineage is provided without forcing every clade into a class rank.

morphology: Egg: usually approximately 30–35 µm, round with a brown radially striated embryophore and a six-hooked oncosphere.
Proglottids and scolex can provide information unavailable in eggs.

transmission.detail: Eating tissue cysticerci produces intestinal taeniasis. Ingestion of T. solium eggs can instead cause tissue cysticercosis.

life_cycle.detail: Cysticerci develop in the intermediate host.
Ingested cysticerci develop into adult tapeworms.

hosts: Humans are definitive hosts of the main human Taenia species; cattle or pigs are intermediate hosts depending on species.
distribution: Worldwide; species and exposure patterns vary across Southeast Asia.
clinical_significance: Intestinal infection often causes mild symptoms or segment passage. A Taenia egg cannot exclude T. solium and its public-health implications.
specimen: Eggs or proglottids in stool; intact segment material may support species confirmation.
diagnostics: Concentration and wet mounts at 400× for striations and hooks.
Segment examination or molecular testing is needed to resolve species.
differential_diagnosis: T. saginata, T. solium and T. asiatica eggs are not reliably separable by light microscopy.
review_status: Source-compiled educational content; not independently clinically validated
description: Taenia spp. — Taeniid tapeworm egg group. Intestinal infection often causes mild symptoms or segment passage. A Taenia egg cannot exclude T. solium and its public-health implications.

annotation_guidance: Record specimen, stage, stain, objective/total magnification, pixel calibration, source image and reviewer certainty.
Native crops of 200–650 pixels do not determine biological size. Retain µm-per-pixel calibration before resizing.
Split training, validation and test data by patient/specimen; keep related crops in the same split.
Keep damaged or ambiguous objects uncertain. Molecular confirmation of a mixed specimen does not assign every pictured object a species.
